summary: Regional attach latency and transient throughput loss caused by background tenant churn
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in the us-west-2 dedicated pools (notably NimbusDocs) experienced elevated p50/p95 attach latency and a 20-40% drop in sustained throughput between 08:30-09:20 UTC. Symptoms correlate with a spike of many short-lived background sessions from a single tenant causing allocator stall and delayed GPU attach handshakes.

Impact:
- NimbusDocs saw sustained request timeouts on batched routes and a 35% reduction in tokens/s for pinned models (gpt-open-7b).
- Other tenants in the same reserved pool observed transient p99 latency increases (~2-4x).
- No host-level GPU crashes; this appears to be allocation/attach contention and autoscaler lag.

Environment:
- prod-us-west-2 dedicated cluster: reserved pool id rp-73b2
- Autoscaler config: cooldown 60s, target_utilization 0.78, predictive disabled
- Runtime build: serving-runtime v2.11.3
- Allocator: gpu-allocator v1.7.0
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a synthetic tenant that opens many short-lived inference streams (2-5s each) across 200 concurrent connections with keepalive disabled.
2) Route those streams into a reserved pool alongside a steady batch workload pinned to gpt-open-7b.
3) Observe GPU attach latencies on the steady workload when background churn reaches ~150 short streams/sec.
4) Toggle autoscaler off and on to reproduce slower recovery vs immediate evictions.

(Attached traces and allocator flamegraphs available in support artifact bundle: s3://redwood-support/sup-214580/trace-attach-20260310.tar.gz)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant short-stream fanout is causing the allocator to hold GPU attach handshake resources and prefetch slots, which blocks steady batch attach attempts and triggers autoscaler hysteresis rather than immediate scale-up.
Evidence: allocator logs show attach_retries spikes aligned to connection bursts; autoscaler decisions included several 'wait' outcomes due to smoothing window.
Other observations: no driver faults or OOMs; NVLink and PCIe metrics normal. Prefetch subsystem shows increased ephemeral KV cache allocations for short streams, increasing memory pressure and attach latency.
Ran targeted repro in staging (rp-staging-12): confirmed 30-40% drop in throughput for co-located steady batch workload under similar short-stream pattern.
Potential causes considered:
- Autoscaler hysteresis too aggressive for mixed short/long workloads
- Allocator serializing attach handshakes when ephemeral stream churn exceeds threshold
- Prefetch subsystem not yielding for background short streams

resolution:
Workaround applied: temporary tenant-side throttling for t-nimbus-21 reduced short-stream churn then autoscaler recovered pool capacity.
Permanent fix plan: (1) Autoscaler tuning: reduce smoothing window and add short-stream-aware sampling; (2) Allocator change: make attach handshake preemption-friendly and introduce attach token quotas per tenant; (3) Sidecar controls: add configurable short-stream rate-limiting and prefetch yielding for ephemeral streams.
Follow-up actions:
- ENG-allocator to open PR for attach token preemption (target: 2026-03-25).
- ENG-autoscaler RFC for mixed-workload heuristics (target: 2026-03-20).
- CS to communicate mitigation steps and recommended client-side keepalive/retry settings to NimbusDocs.
Current status: customer impact mitigated, monitoring in place for 48 hours. Pending change-requests scheduled in product backlog.
notes: Observed that dedicated pools with mixed short/long workload profiles are sensitive to attach token contention. Recommend proactive detection rule in Console to alert when short-stream ratio > 40% of active connections for >5 minutes.
public_updates: 2026-03-12: We applied a targeted throttle to the noisy tenant in us-west-2 which restored throughput for the affected dedicated pool. Engineering is working on scheduler and autoscaler improvements; we'll follow up with schedule for persistent fixes.
